messages:
Alex (VP Eng): Thanks for coming to the all-hands. Quick follow-up: what's our official release cadence now? 2-week sprints company-wide or mixed? I heard different things.

Sam (Eng): Short answer from my team: product = 2-week. infra/platform = monthly. But confusion when a release touches both.

Taylor (Staff SWE): How do we coordinate cross-cutting releases? feature flags? release windows? who owns rollback?

Mira (Product): Also — will PMs be expected to schedule infra changes or does platform own that? Example: KV cache schema change that impacts multiple teams.

Jerome (SRE): From SRE side: infra-first changes should go through the platform release calendar. Requirements: 2-week notice in release plan, at least 24h canary in prod, perf + error SLO verification, and a rollback plan. If a change risks latency SLOs, page oncall immediately.

Olivia (QA): Quality bar question: do we require perf/regression tests in CI for serving/runtime PRs? our current coverage is spotty and we've hit regressions in recent deploys.

Alex (VP Eng): Short answers: 1) Default cadence: product teams -> 2-week sprints; infra/platform -> monthly (or quarterly for big infra projects). 2) Cross-cutting releases: require a release plan on the Release Calendar + feature flags where possible. 3) Oncall rotation: primary = 1 week, secondary = 2 weeks (we'll update docs). 4) Perf QA: yes — any PR that can affect throughput/latency must include a perf checklist and a CI perf run. We'll add automated gating where feasible.

Sam (Eng): Which tracker do we use for the release plan? the 'Release Calendar' board or RFCs?

Alex (VP Eng): Use the Release Calendar board to schedule slots; include an RFC link or a tech spec for details. Example RFC for runtime changes: RFC-345.

Taylor (Staff SWE): RFC-345 link? I couldn't find it in search.

Alex (VP Eng): https://internal.redwood/rfcs/345 — runtime upgrade playbook. Quick checklist to paste into a release plan: 1) release plan in calendar (owner, risk, rollback) 2) canary window (>=24h) 3) perf smoke (CI + synthetic) 4) rollback steps + owner 5) post-deploy monitoring window.

DeployBot: [system] Release window reserved: 2026-04-10 02:00 UTC — slot #43

Mira (Product): Thanks. One more: SLA enforcement — are we moving to stricter latency SLAs for hosted customers? Teams need to know if endpoints must be hardened.

Alex (VP Eng): We'll publish tighter SLAs for new enterprise tiers (target Q3). Existing customers won't see immediate changes. Teams that own endpoints for enterprise must be prepared for smaller error/latency budgets; Redwood Console will expose token-level latency breakdowns to help diagnose.

Jerome (SRE): Action item: I'll update oncall and release docs with the canary + escalation flow and a sample checklist by next Tue.

Olivia (QA): Action item: I'll prototype a CI perf job for the runtime repo and ping engs on Friday for integrations.

Alex (VP Eng): Great. I'll post a short all-hands follow-up with links to RFC-345, the Release Calendar, and the updated oncall doc. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
